chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Hammad al-Harithi, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'No servant supplicates for the believing men and believing women except that Allah will return to him a like [reward] for what he supplicated for them, from every believer and believer who passed away from the beginning of time until the Day of Judgment. And indeed, the servant is ordered to be taken to the Fire, he is dragged [towards it], so the believing men and believing women say: "O our Lord! This is the one who used to supplicate for us, so intercede for him." So Allah will intercede for him through them, and he will be saved from the Fire.'

key_terms.فَیَنْجُو مِنَ النَّارِ: he will be saved from the Fire

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for supplicating for all believers?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the cumulative nature of this reward, noting that the supplicant receives a share from every believer across all eras, creating a vast network of intercessors. This specific mechanism of 'collective intercession' ensures that even if the supplicant is destined for Hell, the prayers of those they blessed can secure their deliverance, emphasizing the communal solidarity of the Shia faithful.
